gates.title: Sonic quality is not yet proven at launch standard
gates.evidence: The documented dontHoldBack proof was rated 4/10 and the current engine has not passed the blind-listening closure gate.
gates.closure_gate: At least 80% of qualified blind listeners prefer ESL over the raw/static baseline on launch benchmark songs.

gates.title: Lead and supporting vocals are not independently proven across the full workflow
gates.evidence: The current proof flow still builds vocals from shared assembly paths and has previously shown doubled, robotic, and missing-vocal behavior.
gates.closure_gate: No unintended duplicate source can enter the sum and every rendered vocal event is traceable to a source region and role.

gates.title: Vocal riding is not yet musical enough for release
gates.evidence: Existing proof logic still relies on global ratio correction and the user reported vocals that were too low, too loud, or hard to hear.
gates.closure_gate: Lead-vocal short-term level stays in the approved pocket without audible pumping or flattened expression.

gates.title: Depth and ambience are not yet modeled as a verified send system
gates.evidence: Current effects are still insert-heavy and have produced dry or phase-like results in proof renders.
gates.closure_gate: Blind listeners identify depth without masking and mono fold-down preserves the lead vocal.

gates.title: Public DSP controls are not fully contract-proven
gates.evidence: Several profile parameters exist before their causal signal effects are verified by contract tests.
gates.closure_gate: Every public control changes the intended signal property and bypass is bit-identical within the defined format.

gates.title: Mastering is still carrying unresolved mix problems
gates.evidence: The current workflow can still arrive at mastering before arrangement, balance, and vocal pocket are fully proven.
gates.closure_gate: Every job stores an approved premaster checkpoint with headroom before mastering begins.

gates.title: Reference matching remains too metric-driven
gates.evidence: A high objective match has already coexisted with a poor human rating, so the current score is not a readiness proof.
gates.closure_gate: Automated quality scores correlate with panel preference and low-confidence results require human review.

gates.title: MixVault learning is not yet quarantined enough for production
gates.evidence: The learning store does not yet enforce consent, quarantine, rollback, and promotion stages as hard gates.
gates.closure_gate: Only approved examples enter the production index and every learned item is traceable, reversible, and consented.

gates.title: Session ingestion still needs deterministic manifest guarantees
gates.evidence: The manifest path now has repeated-render checksum verification in both unit coverage and a real ocean_eyes benchmark fixture, but the closure gate is still open because the full benchmark matrix is not yet enforced.
gates.closure_gate: A deterministic session manifest reproduces the approved arrangement sample-accurately across repeated renders.

gates.title: Backend test coverage is still too shallow for release
gates.evidence: The backend still lacks the breadth of Python unit, integration, golden-audio, and concurrency tests required by the plan.
gates.closure_gate: CI blocks merges on DSP contract failures, timing drift, NaN/Inf, clipping, nondeterminism, API regressions, and benchmark degradation.

gates.title: Frontend breadth exceeds verified depth
gates.evidence: The UI still exposes many partially connected surfaces, so some visible controls remain analysis-only or under-verified.
gates.closure_gate: Every production-visible action has an end-to-end test and auditable effect, or is clearly labeled analysis-only.

gates.title: Preview and offline render parity is not yet demonstrated
gates.evidence: The preview and offline render stacks are still separate enough that equivalent names do not guarantee equivalent output.
gates.closure_gate: Preview/export difference stays below defined tolerances for gain, timing, EQ, dynamics, and automation.

gates.title: Production infrastructure is incomplete or inconsistently documented
gates.evidence: The release story still contains mismatch between claimed readiness and verified deployment surface.
gates.closure_gate: A clean production smoke test completes signup, upload, payment authorization, render, revision, export, deletion, and refund handling.

gates.title: Security and privacy controls still need production verification
gates.evidence: Local-path intake and partial admin protection remain higher-risk than the launch standard requires.
gates.closure_gate: Independent security review and automated tenant-isolation tests pass with no critical or high findings.

gates.title: Legal, rights, and consent rules are not yet enforced as product gates
gates.evidence: Reference ingestion and MixVault learning still need technically enforced consent and deletion boundaries.
gates.closure_gate: Counsel-approved policies match actual behavior and consent plus deletion are technically enforced and tested.

gates.title: Commercial workflow and support are not yet proven end to end
gates.evidence: Billing, revisions, packaging, and client intake exist, but the complete external-order loop has not been proven repeatedly.
gates.closure_gate: Ten consecutive external beta orders complete without manual database repair or lost audio.

release_promise: Constrained multitrack mixing for organized sessions
Reference-assisted workflow with honest A/B comparison
Human-review-backed service when confidence is low

in_scope: Stereo mastering from WAV, AIFF, and FLAC
Organized multitrack mixing for constrained roles
Hip-hop and R&B as validated launch genres
Level-matched A/B proof and engineering reports
Human review fallback when confidence is low
out_of_scope: Automatic comping, pitch correction, or timing repair without approval
Full replacement for Logic, Pro Tools, or a human engineer
Training on customer audio without opt-in
Unlimited genres before genre-specific validation exists

definition_of_market_ready: Preserve intended performance and arrangement decisions
Make the majority of validated songs sound clearly better
Keep vocal results stable, intelligible, dimensional, and artifact-free
Correlate automated confidence with human preference
Prevent bad results from entering production learning
Support safe upload, payment, processing, revision, approval, download, and deletion
Survive retries, worker failures, and browser closure

audit.source: hands-on ESL proof mixing session with Andra
audit.purpose: Persist real-session mix decisions so Echo Sound Lab can reuse them through MixVault, benchmark fixtures, and future reference matching.
global_lessons: Do not render a proof from raw vocal and beat at zero unless timing has been validated against the user's reference bounce.
For session folders with multiple vocal prints, align every candidate to the reference and include intro, bridge, hook, dub, and adlib prints intentionally.
When vocals feel buried, use automated ducking from the vocal envelope before pushing static vocal gain.
A midrange pocket duck is not enough for dense rap vocals; use a small full-band duck plus a focused 1-6 kHz duck.
For Drake/40-style beats, preserve beat weight and depth while keeping consonants forward and section levels even.
For Navy Blue-style warmth, keep the top end less glossy, preserve intimacy, and use low-mid warmth without masking the vocal.
Do not call the studio done until a raw vocal has been mixed, mastered, compared to a reference, revised from feedback, and exported cleanly.
